newsitem.title: GERMANY: Siemens comm unit head to join board.
newsitem.headline: Siemens comm unit head to join board.

text.p: Germany's Siemens AG said on Thursday the head of its public communications unit, Peter Pribilla, would become a member of the group management board.
Pribilla, 55, is to take over responsibility for components and automotive technology on October 1, replacing Walter Kunerth, 56, who is due to leave the company at that time.
Siemens supervisory board recently approved the move, the company said.
In the public communications (ON) unit, one of Siemens fastest growing and most profitable, Pribilla is to be replaced by Roland Koch, who is already member of the ON board.
Siemens also said that group management board member Edward Krubasik would take over responsibility for technology.
The company made no statements about reported plans to shift Chief Financial Officer Karl-Hermann Baumann to the group's supervisory board next year.

Next Monday Siemens planned to report results for the nine-month period ending June 30. In the first six months of 1996/97, ON sales rose 31 percent to 6.3 billion marks ($3.5 billion), while orders increased 52 percent to nine billion marks.
Under Germany's two board system, a management board handles day-to-day operations while a supervisory board made up of management and worker representatives plans long-term strategy.
